title: Compact-to-Hausdorff continuous maps are closed
statement: Let $X,Y$ be topological spaces, with $X$ compact (every open cover has a finite subcover) and $Y$ Hausdorff (distinct points admit disjoint open neighbourhoods). If $f:X\to Y$ is continuous, then for every closed subset $A\subseteq X$ (with its induced topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]) the image $f(A)$ is closed in $Y$. In particular $f(X)$ is closed in $Y$.
